title: Career Roadmap: Researcher
summary: A Researcher investigates questions about society, human behaviour, language, economic systems, public policy and development. Researchers gather evidence, review existing studies, design research methods, analyse data and communicate findings through reports, academic papers, presentations and policy recommendations.

facts.Current degree: Integrated / Dual-Degree Programmes – Integrated MA (Economics / English / Development Studies)

blocks.text: A Researcher investigates questions about society, human behaviour, language, economic systems, public policy and development. Researchers gather evidence, review existing studies, design research methods, analyse data and communicate findings through reports, academic papers, presentations and policy recommendations.

Graduates with an Integrated MA in Economics, English or Development Studies can pursue research careers in universities, policy institutes, think tanks, government projects, non-governmental organisations, consulting firms, publishing organisations and international development agencies.

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Produce credible, systematic and evidence-based knowledge that helps explain social phenomena, evaluate policies, interpret texts or address development challenges.
Major responsibilities

items.text: Identify research questions and define study objectives.
Review academic literature and existing evidence.
Design qualitative, quantitative or mixed-method research.
Collect data through surveys, interviews, documents, experiments or secondary sources.
Analyse evidence using suitable research methods.
Prepare research reports, papers, policy briefs and presentations.
Maintain accurate records, citations and research documentation.
Follow ethical requirements, including consent and data protection.
Collaborate with researchers, institutions and community stakeholders.

The term Researcher covers many different jobs. Some entry-level positions accept a relevant master's degree, while academic research, independent investigator and university faculty roles may require a PhD, publications, specialised methods or eligibility examinations.
The following roadmap assumes a five-year integrated MA programme. Actual programme duration and curriculum vary by institution.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Subject Foundations and Critical Thinking

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Develop strong disciplinary knowledge and the ability to evaluate arguments and evidence.
Study:

items.text: Core concepts in Economics, English or Development Studies.
Research questions and introductory research methods.
Introduction to statistics and data interpretation.
Library research and scholarly database navigation.

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Summarise academic papers or scholarly texts.
Compare different arguments on a research topic.
Identify reliable primary and secondary sources.
Present a research question and explain why it matters.

blocks.label: Year 1 deliverable
blocks.text: A short research paper with a clear question, referenced sources, analytical discussion and limitations.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Research Methods and Evidence Collection

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Learn how to design a study and select appropriate methods.
Study:

items.text: Descriptive statistics and basic statistical inference.
Academic databases and literature search strategies.

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Design a small survey or interview guide.
Prepare a codebook for qualitative data.
Analyse a public dataset or a permitted collection of documents.
Evaluate bias and limitations in a published study.

blocks.label: Year 2 deliverable
blocks.text: A research proposal containing a problem statement, literature review, methods, ethical considerations and a proposed analysis plan.

blocks.label: Year 3
blocks.text: Applied Research and Data Analysis

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Develop practical skills in evidence analysis and research communication.
Study:

items.text: Evidence synthesis and systematic review fundamentals.

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Compare research methods used in different studies.
Produce a research report with tables, charts or coded themes.
Document alternative explanations and sources of uncertainty.

blocks.label: Year 3 deliverable
blocks.text: An applied research project with transparent methods, evidence, findings and limitations.

blocks.label: Year 4
blocks.text: Specialisation and Independent Research

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Build deeper expertise in a chosen research area.
Study:

items.text: Advanced research methods relevant to the specialisation.
Literature synthesis and identification of research gaps.

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Join a faculty research group, policy project or NGO research team.
Analyse a larger dataset or documentary corpus.
Present preliminary findings at a seminar.
Prepare a research paper or policy brief.

blocks.label: Year 4 deliverable
blocks.text: A substantial research project demonstrating independent analytical work and subject expertise.

blocks.label: Year 5
blocks.text: Thesis, Research Internship and Career Preparation

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Demonstrate readiness for research employment or further academic study.
Study:

items.text: Career planning for research organisations and higher education.

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Complete the final thesis or dissertation.
Undertake an internship or research assistantship where available.
Present findings to an academic or professional audience.
Prepare an executive summary or policy brief.
Maintain organised research files and reproducible analysis.
Prepare a research-oriented CV and portfolio.

blocks.label: Year 5 deliverable
blocks.text: A completed thesis, a documented research portfolio and a targeted application package for research positions or doctoral study.
The strongest research career usually builds on the student's main discipline.

blocks.text: Students should select tools based on the research question and the methods used in their discipline rather than attempting to learn every platform.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Structured Literature Review
Choose a narrow topic, search scholarly literature systematically, compare key findings and identify unanswered questions. Document search criteria and source-selection limitations.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Quantitative Data Analysis

Use an appropriate public dataset to answer a focused research question. Clean the data, describe the sample, perform suitable analysis and explain uncertainty and limitations. This is especially relevant for Economics and quantitative Development Studies.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Qualitative or Textual Analysis
Analyse a suitable collection of public documents, literary texts, speeches or policy reports. Define a coding or interpretive framework and support conclusions with carefully selected evidence.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Research Report or Policy Brief
Translate findings into a structured report for a defined audience. Include the research question, methods, evidence, key findings, limitations and practical implications.

If a project involves interviews, surveys or other human participants, obtain the necessary institutional approval and informed consent. Do not publish identifiable or confidential information without proper authorisation.
Seek opportunities that provide direct exposure to research design, data collection, analysis and reporting.
Suitable organisations:

items.text: Economics and public policy think tanks.
Academic publishing and research communications teams.
Language, literature and cultural research centres.

blocks.text: Useful internship responsibilities:
For internships involving communities or sensitive information, prioritise ethical supervision, informed consent and safe data-management practices.
Consider targeted learning in:

items.text: Academic writing and literature review methods.
Digital humanities or corpus linguistics, where relevant.
Monitoring and evaluation for development projects.

blocks.text: Certificates can support learning, but practical research outputs, writing quality and methodological judgement are generally more important for research recruitment.

blocks.text: Job requirements vary. Some research roles require prior fieldwork, specialised software, language skills, quantitative methods or experience with a particular population or policy area.
An Integrated MA may support entry into some research roles, but the next qualification should depend on the intended career.
Potential options include:

items.text: PhD in Economics, English, Development Studies or a related discipline.
Specialised training in econometrics, policy evaluation or statistics.
Advanced qualitative research or ethnographic methods.

blocks.text: A PhD is often important for long-term academic research leadership, faculty appointments and positions requiring independent original research. Many project-based research jobs, however, may accept a relevant master's degree and demonstrated methods experience.

blocks.text: These are indicative pathways rather than guaranteed promotions. Progress depends on research quality, subject expertise, publications, project outcomes, funding and employer requirements.

blocks.label: Impact evaluation

blocks.label: Computational social science
blocks.text: Using computational methods to study social and economic patterns.

blocks.label: Digital humanities

blocks.label: Text and discourse analytics

blocks.label: Climate and development research

blocks.label: AI and society

blocks.label: Open and reproducible research
blocks.text: Improving the transparency and accessibility of research methods and findings.

items.text: Define a clear and answerable research question.
Understand qualitative and quantitative research methods.
Use appropriate analytical tools for the selected discipline.
Interpret evidence critically and acknowledge uncertainty.
Write a clear, properly referenced research report.
Follow research ethics and data-protection requirements.
Complete at least two or three substantial research projects.
Obtain internship or supervised project experience.
Present findings to academic or professional audiences.
Prepare a research CV and writing sample.
Identify whether the target role requires a master's degree, PhD or other specific eligibility.

blocks.text: Final Graduate Profile
A job-ready Researcher should combine critical thinking, research methodology, disciplined evidence collection, analytical ability, academic writing and ethical judgement.

For an Integrated MA graduate, the strongest route is to specialise in Economics, English or Development Studies, build a portfolio of well-designed research projects, gain practical research experience and develop the analytical methods most relevant to the target role. A PhD can provide a pathway to advanced academic research, while master's-level research skills can also support careers in policy, consulting, development organisations and research institutions.
